Linear-light colour spaces, contrast-color() and ctx.lang

I wanted to test three newer colour and text APIs alongside drawElementImage(): linear-light 2D canvas colour spaces (srgb-linear and display-p3-linear), CSS contrast-color() driven by a canvas tint, and CanvasTextDrawingStyles.lang next to drawn CJK DOM text. Drag the sliders, click the neon badges and switch the language to see what your browser supports.

How it works

In an srgb canvas, alpha compositing and ctx.filter = 'blur(...)' average gamma-encoded channel values. Half red plus half cyan ends up at sRGB 0.5, which is only about 21% physical light, so the overlap looks dark and muddy. When the canvas uses srgb-linear or display-p3-linear, the same 50% mix averages linear light and encodes to about 0.73 sRGB, so blurred glows and overlapping neon controls stay bright. Switching between srgb-linear and display-p3-linear replaces the right canvas and calls window.__gfx?.retire() on the old one because a canvas can't change its context attributes after creation.

For the contrast demo, CSS.registerProperty() defines --tint with syntax: '<color>'. The sliders update --tint on the drawable card and request a paint. The canvas paints a gradient backdrop from that colour and draws the card on top, while CSS contrast-color(var(--tint)) picks black or white text based on relative luminance (yellow at 50% lightness flips to black while blue at 50% lightness stays white).

In the third demo, ctx.lang tells Canvas 2D which regional font variant to pick when shaping Han characters that share a Unicode code point across Japanese, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese (直 骨 海 角 刃 令). The canvas copies the computed font size and family from the <span>, draws with ctx.fillText(), and calls drawElementImage() on the <span lang="..."> element right beside it so you can compare strokes directly.

Live checks

These run on small fixtures in the corner of the window. Any pixel inspection copies the drawable canvas into a plain 2D canvas first so a drawable canvas is never read back directly.

Findings

  • Not verified yet in headless Chromium or on Android Chrome 159. The live checks above measure your browser directly when this page opens.
  • To verify linear-light blending: check that getContext('2d', { colorSpace: 'srgb-linear' }) and 'display-p3-linear' report those strings in getContextAttributes().colorSpace, and that overlapping red and cyan drawElementImage() calls measure brighter in srgb-linear than in srgb (around 188 vs 128 in sRGB 8-bit).
  • To verify contrast-color(): check that CSS.supports('color', 'contrast-color(red)') is true and that dragging the lightness slider or tapping Yellow (50%) vs Blue (50%) flips the drawn card's text between black and white.
  • To verify ctx.lang: check that 'lang' in CanvasRenderingContext2D.prototype is true and compare the glyph strokes of 直 骨 海 角 刃 令 between ctx.fillText() and drawElementImage() on a system that has distinct Japanese, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese fonts installed.
